strategy_notes.note: Off-field/suspension risk to an incumbent is a legitimate accelerant for a rookie's snap timeline [FF]: the day-2/day-3 rookie WR base rate (slow starts, second-half relevance) can be overridden when the player ahead of him is under league investigation or otherwise unlikely to be part of the team's future — the org starts developing the rookie sooner. Check the incumbent's status, not just the rookie's draft capital.

Sanctioned buy conditions for a 30+ receiver [Sal]: he normally avoids aging WRs, but names the exact conjunction that overrides it — (a) the target competition in the room has been vacated, (b) a real QB upgrade arrived, and (c) the ADP has already fallen for the age/injury narrative. All three must hold (A.J. Brown, McLaurin, Evans); efficiency stats that survived the down year (YPRR, first downs per route run, zero drops) are the confirmation that the skills, not the situation, are intact.

Four to six games is the read-the-team threshold [FF]: the hosts converge on refusing to judge a team before week 4 and making the call by weeks 4-6 — early enough to still act before the fantasy playoffs, late enough that schedule strength has evened out. They validate the rule against prior-year week-4 standings (Baltimore 1-3, Arizona 2-2 and never winning again) rather than asserting it.

Price an injury backup against the real starter tiers, not the hype [FF]: when a starter goes down and his backup's ADP spikes, ask where the backup would rank if you KNEW he was starting — put him next to the actual committee starters (Tuten, Price, Warren, Stevenson) and see whether you would take him over any of them. That anchor exposed a pick-37 ADP on a day-3 back with no college production on a low-scoring offense. Pair it with the combine-vs-production check (an A.J. Dillon profile: elite athletic testing that never produced in college).

Do not double- and triple-count a risk that is already in the price [Sal]: for aging or injury-prone veterans, age, injury history and a current camp tightness report are often the same risk restated three ways. Once the ADP has fallen to reflect the known profile, an additional narrative ('everybody on that team gets hurt') is not new information and should not produce a further discount. The test is whether the report changes the week-1 availability branch — 25 days to heal with 'not considered serious' does not.

Stale-ADP trap on news-flip players [FF]: an ADP formed during a player's bad-news window (Nabers' ACL recovery pessimism) is already obsolete the moment the news flips, and every manager in the room is staring at that same number hoping for the steal. Never plan a build around the printed ADP of a player whose situation just improved — assume he goes a full round or more earlier than the number says.

Price a stack by naming the players you pass on [FF]: before drafting a stack partner, pull the platform ADP for that exact pick and say out loud who else is on the board. If the opportunity cost is real (DJ Moore in the late fifth costs Jameson Williams / Luther Burden / Tuten / Price), do not force the stack — either wait for a later round where he is free or switch to a cheaper correlated piece (the late-round TE version of the same stack).

Camp reception counts by quarterback as a target-pecking-order proxy [FF]: they explicitly want, for every team, the full ordered list of how many catches each pass catcher made from the starting QB across training camp — and treat that ordering as real signal while dismissing preseason completion percentage as noise ('they should be failing in preseason'). It is a usage metric available before any snap chart exists, and it resolved their New England pecking order (Brown > Doubs > Stevenson > Douglas > Henry > Boutte).

Three-outcome (wild-card) classification and its roster cap [FF]: sort picks into 'guaranteed to produce on some level' vs wild cards whose range genuinely spans worthless / flex-worthy / league-winning, and deliberately carry only one or two wild cards on a roster — 'you really don't want a bunch of those'. The classification is also a filter for hype: a player who cannot plausibly reach the league-winning end (Bucky Irving with the pass-catching role gone, R.J. Harvey behind two names) does not belong in the bucket regardless of how exciting he is.
Anchor with elite RBs: two RBs in your first three picks (reliability, not breakout swings) — RBs fly early this year and the position is barren by round 5.

The RB dead zone is back — RB24 now costs a 5th-round pick (a 7th in 2024) — grab two elite backs in the first 3-4 rounds and refuse to pay for middling RB2/3s (Etienne, Montgomery, Warren, Pollard all priced above projection).
Elite QB prices are the cheapest in years — Lamar a full round-plus cheaper than last year's QB2; Burrow (rd 5) / Daniels and Hurts (rd 6) are legitimate value even for late-round-QB drafters.
Wait on QB in 1QB: Allen is the lone QB priced in round 2 while Daniels/Hurts/Maye deliver comparable upside ~50 picks later; rounds 10-11 are the last window for Kyler/Mahomes/Purdy types.
Avoid RBs on bad teams: backs on sub-7-win teams hit ADP only ~30% of the time; 2026 teams that are underdogs in 3+ of their first 4 (ARI, CLE, IND, LV, MIA, NYJ, DEN) create uphill starts.
Don't stash day-2/3 rookie WRs early (48%/30% snaps, 2-4 targets through week 6) — only first-round rookies start day one; spend late picks on backup RBs whose value transfers predictably.

The old-WR cliff is the worst bet on the board: the 10 oldest drafted players beat ADP just 30% of the time and old WRs only 21% — this year that's Adams and Evans — with encore-effect exceptions (Henry, Kelce, Stafford).

Tight end is elite-or-punt: pay for Bowers/McBride/Loveland/Warren or wait for late profiles with 17%+ target share and 15%+ air-yard share (Likely, Goedert, Kincaid, Juwan Johnson) — mid-round TEs waste RB/WR upside picks.

Middle-round RB and middle-round TE are the two worst-priced blocks on the 2026 board [FF/Jason] — 'the opportunity cost is too great' there this year. The paired swing: late-round QB has gone so far out of fashion that QBs are falling past their value, so the current edge is the middle-round QB, not the last-round one. Strategy rotates every couple of years as ADP self-corrects; the job is to find whichever block the market has mispriced THIS season, not to re-run last year's rule.

Sleeper-definition inflation [FF]. With ADP now accurate front-to-back and the average manager far more informed, a genuine sleeper can no longer be a known player at a modest discount — it has to be a player where 'right now it seems impossible' and the honest base rate is near-total failure. Corollary they apply on the same breath: late-round shots must go to players you believe are actually GOOD, because 'there are late-round guys who just stink' and opportunity alone on a bad player is a wasted ticket. This is the same bar our league_winners screen enforces.

Dynasty horizon is three years, not ten [FF]. They rejected their own 10-year 'who would you take' question on principle: player trajectories are not forecastable past ~3 years, so dynasty value should be argued on a three-year window. Directly relevant to our never-cut-youth rule — a young stash's thesis should be defensible inside three seasons, not on an indefinite 'someday'.
Never put an early-week (Wed/Thu) player in a FLEX slot; put him in his positional slot so the flex stays open to cover Sunday injuries or news.

Kicker selection: prefer a good kicker on a mediocre offense that settles for 40-60 yard field goals and rarely goes for it on 4th down; avoid kickers on aggressive TD-heavy offenses (DET, LAR, DAL) even if they're better real-life kickers.
Use Vegas player props (reception O/U) as a trustworthy read on a player's expected Week-1 usage; big money keeps those lines tight.
When a team refuses to say where a player's 'soreness' is, read it as PR cover for the previously injured joint (e.g. the knee for a two-time ACL back) — a red flag, not noise.
The days before Week 1 are the peak sell-high window for camp-hype players: benchmark offers against real trades happening in other leagues that week and convert hype into proven target-earners.
Draft capital a team spends to acquire a player reveals its valuation: a 2028 6th-rounder for Kaleb Johnson means RB3, not a real competitor.
Explosive-play seasons regress: 1,000 yards on ~84 targets (18% share) is not repeatable; target share is the sustainable driver (Saquon's 2024-to-2025 as the RB analogue).
A bad offensive line hits inexperienced running backs first; check consensus O-line rankings before buying a new RB1.
Historical base rate: no NFL running back has returned productive from back-to-back ACL tears; lean on the history rather than betting against it.
A QB returning from an Achilles loses downfield power (Cousins, Rodgers precedents), which specifically hurts his deep-threat WR while pushing volume to short-area TE/RB options.
A bottom-5 offense craters even elite-talent pass catchers (ARI 2025 with McBride/Harrison); QB situation can turn a 2nd-round WR into 5th-round value.
New-regime discount: a coaching staff with no draft-capital or money attachment to a player (Skattebo, 4th-round pick) will not force-feed him; check who the new staff signed.
Week 1 for last-round stashes is a usage read, not a points read: track snap share (75%+ = full starter), routes and targets, then either punt them on the first waiver wire or hold with conviction.

Depth-chart order does not predict who takes over after an injury; evaluate the more talented backup (Ollie Gordon over Jaylen Wright, Jonah Coleman over RJ Harvey, Vidal behind Hampton) rather than the listed RB2.

Prefer insurance backs with standalone weekly touches (Corum, Brooks, C-Rod, Monangai, Allgeier, Gainwell) over pure handcuffs; early-season handcuffs with zero standalone value cost you waiver churn.
Only ~24% of top-24 RBs survive 17 weeks — plan on injuries at RB and size handcuff/FAAB accordingly; but don't full-FAAB a backup on a bad offense (Miami) because he won't be a top-10 RB anyway.
Rookie WR base rate: non-high-first-round rookies start slow; only stash the ones projected for 75%+ snaps from Week 1.

TE age curve differs from RB/WR: tight ends are routinely fine at 31-33 (especially TD-dependent ones) without being Hall of Famers; athleticism matters more at TE than any position and TE breakouts often take 4-6 years.
Update conclusions when the data changes (court date moved two months = shorter absence); don't hold a take after its premise moves.
Last-pick IR trick: draft an IR-eligible player (Pacheco, Tyson) with the final pick, move him to IR, and add a free flier — an extra roster spot for nothing.
Week 1 tiebreakers: defenses are ahead of offenses so expect low totals; home favorites get the RB start/sit nod in coin flips; don't overreact to Week 1 results.
Ignore platform Week-1 projections and draft grades: platforms exist to run leagues, not to project players; historically an A grade is a warning and a D/F often means a great team.

Off-field/discipline risk in dynasty: discount a player whose value is team-specific (Rashee Rice) more than one whose skill translates anywhere (Nacua) — the latter gets paid by a WR-needy team even if his current team walks.
Players on the commissioner's exempt list can't go to IR — the stash costs a real bench spot for as long as the case runs.

Played 6 of 10 Jets first-team snaps (60%) versus one snap for Isaiah Williams — a full reversal of the previous week — but is still the 4th or 5th option behind Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq.
6'5", 218 lb third-round rookie out of Notre Dame with college target shares of 25%, 23% and 20%; played all 8 Giants starter snaps then was pulled after the first drive.
The 2026 NFL season kicks off Wednesday, September 9 — five days later than 2025, shifting the busiest draft weekend later than usual. New England plays that first game.

Dynasty panic trades executed during the Jeanty injury window included the Raiders' backup RB for Blake Corum; the backup plus a first for Jalen Waddle; a 2027 second straight up; and the backup straight up for Brian Thomas Jr.
Kyren Williams split the Rams backfield nearly 50-50 with Blake Corum over the back half of last season and into the postseason.
Was a top-five pass-catching RB in all receiving categories last season with the Steelers.

All preseason snap-count charts Sal grades from are PFF's; he is not affiliated with them. He won 75% of his home leagues last season including the Flock League ($10,000 first prize) against an expert field.
Led the Falcons in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards last season — the only other NFL TE to do that for his team was Trey McBride; 63% of his targets came under 10 yards.
Tenth overall pick who led the Bears in receiving yards as a 21-year-old rookie TE — first rookie TE to do that for the franchise since Mike Ditka.

Over the Bears' final four games he saw 49 targets with four straight double-digit-target games, was targeted on 35% of his routes, had 7 red-zone targets, and caught 8 for 137 and a TD in the wild card vs GB.
One of only five players ever to begin a career with three straight 80-catch, 1,000-yard seasons, done with eight different QBs; 28% target share over four seasons and 30% last year in seven games.
Was WR5 before his injury last year with four top-15 finishes in the first five weeks; excluding TDs he was on pace for 112 receptions and 1,300 yards.
The Jets passing offense failed to reach 2,800 team passing yards last year — only one other team in the last decade threw for fewer yards per game.
The 27%+ target-share group drafted in the top 12 is JSN, Chase, Nacua, St. Brown, Jefferson, London, Flowers, A.J. Brown and Olave — Garrett Wilson is the lone member going around WR20.
33rd overall pick, 6'2" 207, 4.36 combine; averaged 84 receiving yards per game over his last five college games; has broken every record for preseason target share by a rookie.
Since 2019 at least four rookie WRs have finished inside the top 36 every year, except last year when only two did.
Signed a three-year deal worth up to $45 million with Kansas City — the fifth-highest fully guaranteed RB contract in the league.
Kansas City was dead last in explosive rush rate last year with one 20+ yard run as a team, tied for fewest 20+ yard plays that scored (four), and dead last in forced missed tackle rate.

Had 10 runs of 20+ yards last year, 15% of carries went for 10+ (third best among RBs), No. 1 among RBs in forced missed tackle rate; in three playoff games 74 touches for 417 scrimmage yards, 23.4 fantasy PPG.
From 2004 to 2018 Andy Reid's RB1 averaged 22 opportunities per game, 110 total yards per game and nearly 20 PPR points per game.
Lead backs on teams with a 10.5-win total average over 1,250 total yards and 10.5 TDs; the Chiefs are favored in all of their first five games with a week 5 bye.

Drafted 4th overall; led the nation in passer rating when targeted, 875 yards and nine TDs in a season sharing the field with Jeremiah Smith, five TDs of 40+, caught 12 of 14 contested targets, never dropped a pass; 5 targets and 0 receptions in the preseason.
Preseason lines for established stars: Ja'Marr Chase 1 reception on 5 targets, Drake London 1 catch on 1 target, A.J. Brown 1 catch on 3 targets.

Per a Ryan Heath (Fantasy Points) correlation chart, completion percentage is one of the lowest-correlating QB stats to next-season fantasy PPG, while avoided sacks correlates roughly three times as strongly.

Had the 4th-most end-zone pass attempts in the league, dropped 15 pounds this offseason, ADP is QB7 — the same finish as last year; the Bears jumped from 28th to 9th in points per game in year one under Ben Johnson. 60% of first-round QBs who finished top-10 in year two topped 20 fantasy PPG in year three.

One of only three WRs since 2000 to average 17+ yards per reception with 20 TDs through their first four years; from week 11 on last year he was WR11, 2nd in yards per route run, tied 3rd in targets per route run and 1st in the NFL in first downs per route run; out-route rate went from 7.7% in 2022-24 to 35% last year (Josh Norris). Just signed a four-year extension.

Among 38 qualifying QBs with 200+ dropbacks, Jordan Love was 1st in EPA with a clean pocket, 6th in passer rating, 7th in CPOE and 4th in pressure-to-sack ratio, while the Packers ranked 28th in pass rate.

Took 80% of the goal-line carries last year (would have ranked 4th in the NFL), averaged 19 routes and 3.6 receptions per game, and led all RBs in avoided tackles per carry over the first five weeks before his injury.
12 of 15 first-round running backs in their second season averaged 18 or more opportunities per game, with those players averaging 10.3 touchdowns.

One of seven WRs in the last decade with 200+ targets, 1,900 receiving yards and 13 TDs through two seasons — every player who has ever done it was a top-24 pick the following year. His sophomore drop was six fewer targets with a collapsed catch rate; 4th in yards per route run on go routes.
Keenan Allen was the Chargers' leading receiver last year and is now gone.
Jonathan Taylor was 3rd in the NFL in routes run last year (~25/game) and 3rd in route rate (74% of dropbacks).
Bills OC Pete Carmichael said he wants James Cook to 'bring value in the run and pass game' this year and floated an expanded receiving role depending on game plan/matchup.

Chase Brown averaged 19.4 fantasy ppg over his final 6 games last year once Joe Burrow returned, and has averaged ~20 fantasy ppg (nearly 100 total yards/game) in every extended stretch dating to 2024 when Burrow was healthy.

Derrick Henry had nearly 1,600 rushing yards on 300+ carries last year at 5.2 yards/carry, top-10 in the NFL in yards/touch (5.4) and 11th in true yards/carry (4.8) despite defenses selling out to stop the run.
Kenneth Walker missed practice this week with a foot injury, about 2.5 weeks before Week 1; severity was undetermined as of the recording (2026-08-27).

Ashton Jeanty's ankle sprain is described by the team as 'more low than high,' but Adam Schefter separately characterized it as 'not long-term but not good'; teams aren't required to disclose injury grade until week-1 practice reports.
Javonte Williams had 62 red-zone touches (top-5 among RBs) and 51 targets (11th among RBs) last year, and is one of just 5 RBs projected for 10+ touchdowns this year.

New Orleans' backfield behind Travis Etienne is almost entirely hurt heading into week 1: Alvin Kamara (MCL sprain, could miss the start of the season), Devine Ozigbo (re-injured hamstring), and Ty Chandler (feared season-ending injury in camp).
Reports since May 2026, reaffirmed again in mid-August training camp, consistently describe Kyren Williams and Blake Corum heading for a roughly 50/50 rushing split.
Josh Jacobs missed all of training camp with a groin injury while backup MarShawn Lloyd (younger, bigger, more explosive) stayed healthy and looked good.

Rookie RB Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a high ankle sprain that has cost him essentially all of training camp; James Conner and Tyler Allgeier are both ahead of him on the depth chart to start the year.

D'Andre Swift's top backfield competition suffered a hyperextended knee in training camp, reportedly set to miss multiple weeks; Swift himself posted ~1,400 total yards and 10 TDs last year, top-10 in true yards/carry and top-8 in yards/touch (5.4).
Woody Marks played all 10 snaps with the 1st-team offense (C.J. Stroud) in a preseason game David Montgomery sat out, turning 5 touches into 43 yards and a touchdown.
Zach Charbonnet had ACL surgery in February 2026, which caps how early he can realistically return regardless of optimistic team language.

Jacksonville's RB committee is reportedly structured as: Bhayshul Tuten starts drives (early-down/lead role), LeQuint Allen worked third downs before his injury, and Chris Rodriguez gets red-zone/goal-line touches inside the 10-yard line.
Since 2019, at least 4 rookie WRs have finished inside the top 36 in fantasy scoring every single year except one (only 2 did last year).

Rico Dowdle's usage and output were nearly identical across two different seasons on two different teams: 284 opportunities / 235 carries / 1,079 yards / 39 receptions / 2 TDs in Dallas (2024) vs. 286 opportunities / 236 carries / 1,076 yards / 39 receptions / 6 TDs in Carolina (2025) -- only the touchdown total varied.

A Steelers beat writer (name rendered in captions as 'Mark Cavalee') states Rico Dowdle will be the Steelers' 'unquestioned RB1' when the season starts, even though the team's official depth chart and both 2026 preseason games have listed Jaylen Warren ahead of him and Warren has taken the first offensive snap both times.
Alec Pierce came off the PUP list on 2026-08-27. The Colts open the 2026 season against the Ravens, Chiefs and Texans.

Green Bay signed a veteran tight end to a one-year deal as depth insurance; incumbent Luke Musgrave has been dealing with a significant abdomen injury reported ~4 days before this episode (2026-08-27). The hosts said this doesn't change their outlook on Tucker Kraft.
facts.about: Green Bay Packers tight end room

facts.fact: Malik Nabers left practice early on 2026-08-27, walking off with a trainer about 20 minutes before the session ended; the team clarified afterward that the early departure was unrelated to injury.

Mike Evans has overlapping lower-body issues this camp (quad, groin, hamstring language all used) and states he plans to play week 1, but the hosts expect a genuinely inconsistent, partial-season workload even while he remains a dominant per-game scorer when active.
Zay Flowers has been held out of practice for 'precautionary reasons' and is still expected to be ready for week 1.
Travis Etienne's departure leaves over 300 touches from the 2025 Jacksonville offense up for grabs.
Chris Rodriguez entered 2026 training camp with a foot injury, hoping to be ready by Week 1; he offers nothing in the passing game and is not explosive.
Tyler Warren finished as a top-10 fantasy tight end in 2025 and ranked 3rd overall in tight end targets, despite his quarterback getting hurt in Week 13.
Michael Pittman's 111 targets from 2025 are gone from the Indianapolis offense.
Rashee Rice led the NFL in both red-zone target rate and designed target rate in 2025.
Over the last two seasons, Rashee Rice has produced as a top-5 fantasy wide receiver in the games he has played.
Kansas City brought back an aging Travis Kelce and Tyquan Thornton and let Marquise Brown go, adding no new target competition for Rashee Rice.
Kyler Murray is being drafted around the QB10-11 range despite being named Minnesota's Week 1 starter.

Josh Jacobs was formally charged with two misdemeanors stemming from the May arrest — misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property (Tom Pelissero) — with a court appearance scheduled for November 17.

The NFL CBA minimum suspension for domestic abuse is six games, and that minimum applies in a felony circumstance; Jacobs was not charged with felonies and the counts were not classified as domestic violence.
A garage surveillance video was a component of the charges against Josh Jacobs; if it reaches the public, the commissioner's exempt list becomes an immediate in-season risk.

Expected legal calendar for Josh Jacobs (per Drew Davenport's read): the Nov 17 appearance is a not-guilty plea with a waived speedy trial, pushing an actual trial to January or February — so absent a video leak, a 2026-season suspension is unlikely and the hosts' bet is roughly four missed games in 2027.
Green Bay's contingency ladder behind Josh Jacobs: MarShawn Lloyd is the direct insurance back and would be the starter; Chris Brooks is the insurance back behind Lloyd.
Javonte Williams was drafted as the RB39 last year and finished as the RB11 — the template for the 'RB drafted outside the top 24, attached to a good offense' screen.

Houston converted about 17% of their attempts inside the five-yard line last year, then acquired a goal-line back and committed to David Montgomery in that role; the Texans are favored in six of their first seven games before the bye.

12-team ADPs cited for the three 'outside the top-24 RB' picks: Jadarian Price 5.11 (overall ~59), Bhayshul Tuten 6.01 (overall ~61, RB25), David Montgomery 6.11 (overall ~71, RB26 and the latest of the three).

Seattle's Hard Knocks premiere shows GM John Schneider calling running back the team's biggest need in the draft room; George Holani, the only competition for Jadarian Price, has roughly 25 career touches.

Bhayshul Tuten last year converted 5 of his 7 carries inside the five-yard line into touchdowns; among 55 qualifying running backs he was 5th in rush success rate, 5th in percentage of yards after contact, and tied for 11th with Breece Hall in forced missed tackle rate.
Jacksonville's other backfield variables are Chris Rodriguez at the goal line and LeQuint Allen on receiving downs.
Trevor Lawrence was drafted as the QB21 last year and finished as the QB4 — the template for the late-round QB screen (outside the top 12, new OC or upgraded weapons, rushing floor).

55% of Kyler Murray's 82 career starts have been top-12 QB performances; he is being drafted as the QB17 in the 13th round (12-team). Counterpoint raised on the show: in his five healthy games last year he averaged 35 rushing yards per game and still never finished as a top-15 QB.

Tyler Shough over weeks 14-18 last year completed 70% of his passes, averaged 27 rushing yards per game and 20 fantasy points per game; among 28 rookie QBs with 100+ pass attempts over the past five years he ranks 2nd in completion rate, 4th in passing yards per game and 6th in yards per attempt. He is being drafted as the QB22.

Baker Mayfield was the QB3 in 2024 with 378 rushing yards and ran for 382 yards last year; he was the QB4 through the first six weeks of last season before the Mike Evans, personal and offensive-line injuries; he is not under contract for next season and opens week 1 at Cincinnati with a 51.5 over/under.

Michael Wilson went undrafted in fantasy drafts last year and finished as the WR11 — the template for the 'non-rookie WR buried on a depth chart who breaks out' screen; his opportunity arrived only when Marvin Harrison Jr. was injured.

Jalen Coker had four top-24 weekly finishes in his final seven games last year and put up 9 catches on 12 targets for 134 yards and a touchdown in Carolina's playoff loss to the Rams; he is healthy and was rewarded with a three-year contract extension. He goes in the 13th-14th round or undrafted.

Dontayvion Wicks' targets per route run: 23% in 2023, 30% in 2024, 21% in 2025 — over the last three years a higher per-route target rate than Zay Flowers, Christian Watson or George Pickens. Now traded to Philadelphia and locked in by beat reporters as the No. 2 opposite DeVonta Smith with A.J. Brown gone; ADP is WR73.
Beat reporters say Jack Bech has won the Raiders' starting slot role and that he is a better fit in Kubiak's system; Bech has 20 career receptions to date.
TreVeyon Henderson should be good to go for week 1 (Boston Globe).
Isiah Pacheco's knee injury is not a concern to Dan Campbell, but he is now dealing with a back issue as well.
There were rumors that a suspension for Puka Nacua was imminent; Sean McVay said specifically that Nacua's absence was not related to that.
Jordyn Tyson's injury is significant enough that the hosts pulled back on Tyler Shough; the Shough thesis is explicitly staged around Tyson returning in the second half of the season.

The Jets did not reach 2,800 team passing yards last year — only one other team in the last decade gained fewer passing yards per game, and the second-worst passing team last year (Cleveland) threw for 400 more yards than they did.
Jordan Love finished as the QB5 in fantasy three years ago at just under 19 points per game, before Josh Jacobs arrived; his QB production dropped over the past two years with Jacobs.
Green Bay ranked number one in rushing and 28th in passing, which caps Jordan Love's passing volume; the hosts say he needs ~35 passing TDs to matter for fantasy because he doesn't run.

Commissioner's exempt list precedent cited from a Connor Allen tweet: Julius Peppers 47 days; Adrian Peterson 15 games; Greg Hardy 15 games; Reuben Foster 5 games; Kareem Hunt 5 games; Jabrill Peppers 7 games. Some players placed on the list never played again.
The minimum NFL suspension for a domestic violence situation is six games.
The charges filed against Josh Jacobs were REDUCED from the original arrest, and the NFL put him on the exempt list a few days AFTER those charges came out.
Jacobs' court case is scheduled to be heard in November, but per Drew Davenport that court date is irrelevant to the NFL's process/timeline.
Josh Jacobs cannot be placed on fantasy IR while on the commissioner's exempt list — he occupies an active bench spot.
The Fantasy Footballers moved MarShawn Lloyd to roughly RB24-RB30 in their UDK rankings within a day of the Jacobs news (one host has him about RB24), and re-ranked the entire Packers offense.
Green Bay has been running more vertical wide zone; beat reporters questioned how Josh Jacobs fit that scheme, while MarShawn Lloyd (and Kaleb Johnson) fit it.
MarShawn Lloyd was a third-round NFL draft pick by Green Bay (NFL draft round, not fantasy).

Keenan Allen was arrested Sunday morning and charged with DWI and DWI endangering a person; he was under 0.08 and was in a parked vehicle, not driving. Per Drew Davenport the legal situation won't be resolved until the end of the year.
Kyle Pitts had a 37-yard run up the sideline in the final preseason game, escaping the defense.
'McKay Lemon' (ASR; likely Makai Lemon), a first-round rookie WR, played in the final preseason game and had 3 catches for 3 yards plus a drop that turned into an interception.
'Xavier Thomas' (ASR-uncertain), a Bears wide receiver, ran a 4.28 at about 190 pounds and showed that speed in preseason.
Cyrus Allen played behind Xavier Worthy, Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton in the final KC preseason game, despite a strong camp drumbeat and reports he was working exclusively with Mahomes.
Dallas waived all of their backup running backs other than Malik Davis — Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah both gone.
Zach Charbonnet will remain on the PUP list to start the season.
The undrafted back behind Jadarian Price (ASR 'Helani', likely George Holani) has touched the ball roughly 25 times in his career.
Rookie RB Adam Randall was placed on short-term IR by Baltimore (four-game absence), after looking very good in preseason.
Season-opening IR placements named: Jordyn Tyson, Tank Dell, James Conner, Christian Kirk. Arizona also waived Trey Benson injured.
Puka Nacua returned to practice on Sunday after dealing with a hip flexor.
Todd Bowles reported he is hopeful Emeka Egbuka will be ready for week 1; Egbuka is recovering from turf toe.
Jeremiyah Love's ankle is probably good to go.
Luther Burden looks 100% according to Ben Johnson.

Cutdown-day waivers named: Will Levis, Jaydon Blue, Phil Mafah, 'Demarcato' waived by the Chiefs, Jaleel McLaughlin waived by the Broncos, Jonah Coleman, Damien Pierce waived by the Eagles, Greg Dortch left the Lions, Jalen Hyatt cut.
Odell Beckham Jr. is a member of the Giants, and Jalen Hyatt — who wore his number — is no longer on the team.
Sean Tucker agreed to a one-year deal with Tampa Bay and was not cut; his $3.5M deal was reduced to $2.5M at the end of training camp. He had been tendered.
Aaron Donald is returning, with his deal going from $20 million up to $30 million, joining a roster that also has Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams and Myles Garrett.
The last 20 teams favored by this wide a Super Bowl margin went 0-20 (as cited by the hosts).
Host odds that Wandale Robinson finishes as Tennessee's fantasy WR1: 3%, 15% and 35% across the three hosts.
In their 18-team chopped/guillotine league, teams got chopped regularly in the weeks their stars were on bye (Jonathan Taylor's bye week named as an example).
One host took Josh Jacobs in their chopped league before the news broke, and considers that roster already effectively eliminated.
Kenneth Walker III signed with the Chiefs this offseason for almost $30 million and is being drafted at the end of the second round; Isaiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt are both gone.
Patrick Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL and the Chiefs are hinting they want to run more.
Sam LaPorta has been a top-8 fantasy TE every single year of his career and is going around the eighth round, behind Harold Fannin.
Brock Purdy is available in round 9; he has averaged a top-12 weekly QB finish when on the field and posted 30- and 40-point games last year.
Mike Evans is top-5 in wide receiver efficiency over the last two seasons when on the field, and is Purdy's first true X receiver since 2023.

A.J. Brown has averaged over 1,200 receiving yards per year for the last four years and was still top-10 in PPR points per game last season in a broken Eagles offense; he is going at the end of round 2 and his new WR room is Kayshon Boutte, Romeo Doubs and Demario Douglas.
A.J. Brown's four-year Eagles average was 131 targets, 85 catches and 1,200+ receiving yards, a top-12 fantasy WR finish every year (seasons: ~1,500, 1,400+, 1,000, 1,000).
Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list (reported by Adam Schefter); he can't play while listed but still gets paid, and there is allegedly a video the NFL has seen.
Josh Jacobs had 300+ carries two years ago and 234 carries last year while dealing with injuries, seeing 16-20+ touches a game; he dealt with a groin injury for most of this camp.

MarShawn Lloyd is available in over 70% of leagues and is priced by Sal in the Rhamondre Stevenson / Jaylen Warren / Rico Dowdle range — a 6th-to-7th round target, with 4th-5th round drafting called a complete mistake.
MarShawn Lloyd injury log: 2024 hamstring, then an ankle sprain in week 2 on return, then appendicitis; last year a hamstring that ended his season entirely.
MarShawn Lloyd at USC: 111 and 116 rush attempts in a shared backfield in his final year, 7.1 yards per carry, 820 rushing yards, averaging 10 TDs per season, limited as a pass catcher.
MarShawn Lloyd ran 4.46 at 220 lbs (93rd percentile speed for combine RBs) and is 87th percentile in bench press.
Green Bay traded a 2028 sixth-round pick to Pittsburgh for Caleb Johnson, the Steelers' third-round rookie; he projects as the Packers RB3 behind Lloyd and Chris Brooks (who is on the NFI list).

Packers offense described as maybe the thinnest in the NFL: lost Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks; starters are Matthew Golden (did nothing last year), Christian Watson (never more than 11 games in a season) and Jayden Reed (coming off injury, mostly slot); Tucker Kraft coming off a torn ACL; no backup QB; average-at-best offensive line.
FAAB guidance on MarShawn Lloyd: 50-70% in a 10- or 12-team league with 14-15 rounds and short benches; up to 100% in a deep/competitive league like the Flock League.

The Denver rookie RB (ASR-garbled name) is available in 95% of leagues, is a ~13th round pick, weighs 220 lbs, and in college had 758 yards and 17 TDs in his final year at Washington after a 1,000-yard, 10-TD breakout the year before.

That Denver rookie's college profile: 71% of rushing yards came after contact (1st in his class), 1st in yards per carry and first-down rate when hit behind the line of scrimmage, and one fumble on 630+ career college touches.

Sean Payton pulled the Denver rookie RB early in preseason week 1, saying 'I didn't need to see additional evidence of what I've already been seeing for 3 weeks in camp,' and has not played him in the preseason since.
facts.about: UNRESOLVED Broncos rookie RB / Sean Payton

facts.fact: J.K. Dobbins has not played more than 13 games in a season in four years: missed 7 games last year, 5 the year before, 16 the year before that, 9 the year before that, plus a game the year before that — at least five games missed in each of the last four seasons.

R.J. Harvey averaged about 14 fantasy points per game filling in for Dobbins last year but ran 3.4 yards per carry (65th in the NFL) and ranked 34th in yards per touch; he is listed at roughly 200-205 lbs.
Denver has one of the best offensive lines in the league, one of the best offenses and a great defense, so they play with a lead.

The 49ers' rookie RB (ASR 'Kayln/Ke'Shawn Black') is available in 93% of leagues, goes undrafted as RB58 / 190th overall, is 208 lbs with a 4.51 forty, and was a third-round pick out of Indiana after transferring from James Madison; he is 24 turning 25 next year.

That 49ers rookie's Indiana production: 187 carries, 1,000 yards, 10 TDs; playoff run of 15 carries/99 yards/6.6 YPC/1 TD, 63 yards and 2 TDs vs Oregon, 17 carries/79 yards in the title game vs Miami; only four catches per season in his last two Indiana years after a 27-reception season at James Madison.
Christian McCaffrey is 30 years old, is coming off 400+ touches last year, and has already dealt with tightness in training camp.
In 2024, in the five games McCaffrey missed to start the year with Jordan Mason healthy, Mason averaged 17 fantasy points, 21 carries and 107+ rushing yards per game.

Jordan James is still recovering from fractured ribs but is expected back for week 1; Hayden Winks credited the 49ers' third-round rookie with winning the RB2 job in preseason week 2 on two great pass-protection reps versus blitzers plus vision.
Woody Marks is available in 63% of leagues and goes 139th overall, after kickers.
Woody Marks was a fourth-round rookie with 900+ total yards last year: 700 rushing, 208 receiving, 6 TDs — but 3.5 yards per carry (61st in the NFL) and 4.1 yards per touch (50th).

Woody Marks college receiving line across five years (Mississippi State/USC): 60, 83, 48, 23 and 47 catches, and 1,100 rushing yards with 9 TDs in his last college years; his postseason breakout was 19 carries for 112 yards and a TD against Pittsburgh's defense.
Woody Marks opened a preseason game with the starters: four carries for 37 yards and a 20-yard rushing TD, plus a reception. Sal estimates he plays at least 35% of the time.

Zane Dailey (beat) reports David Montgomery and Woody Marks have been used nearly evenly throughout camp, with the Marks tape and coach-speak all positive; the split may not be 50-50 but will be close.
Chris Rodriguez Jr. is available in 52% of leagues and goes 128th overall (an 11th-round pick in 12-team formats).

Over the final six games last season Chris Rodriguez Jr. led that backfield with 14.2 carries and 63+ rushing yards per game and five TDs in six games, while the rookie he was competing with (ASR 'J.D. McKissic') averaged 25-30 rushing yards and 4-5 fantasy points per game.
Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s 2021 season at Kentucky under Liam Coen: 225 carries, 1,300 rushing yards, 6.1 YPC, 13 TDs.

On rush attempts inside the 5-yard line over the last two seasons, Chris Rodriguez Jr. is 1st in the NFL in yards per carry, 4th in success rate, top-3 in yards after contact per attempt, and 1st in EPA per rush.

Zane Dailey reported Rodriguez and Tank Bigsby took roughly equal reps at Wednesday's practice, but Rodriguez got the end-of-game and pass-protection reps in joint practice, and is getting the red-zone touches in camp.
The RB the Jaguars lost (ASR names him 'Antonio Gibson') left behind nearly 1,400 yards and an RB13 overall fantasy finish from last season.
facts.about: Jacksonville vacated backfield (departed RB name ASR-garbled)

facts.fact: Caleb Douglas is a Dolphins third-round rookie out of Texas Tech, available in 96% of leagues; 6'4", 206 lbs, ran a 4.3-range forty with an elite speed score; ~20% target share in each of his last two college years with 800+ yards and six TDs in each.

In preseason week 2 Malik Willis and the Dolphins starters played 14 snaps; Caleb Douglas was the only WR on the field for 100% of them and drew two targets, Malik Washington played 12 of 14, and no other WR played more than two snaps (Chris Bell was inactive).
Alex Cups (Cups Analytic) lists Caleb Douglas's rookie comps as Allen Robinson, Terry McLaurin, Pat Bryant, Dante Moore(?), DK Metcalf, Kenny Golladay and Cedric Tillman.
Malik Washington had 65 targets last year for only 317 yards, with an average target depth of 5.1 yards downfield — 96th in the NFL.

Miami's WR room turnover: Tyreek Hill is an unsigned free agent and still injured, Jaylen Waddle was traded to the Broncos for a first-round pick, Nick Westbrook signed with the Colts, Tutu Atwell was signed then traded back to the Rams for RB Jarquez Hunter, Jalen Tolbert was brought in, and Miami drafted three WRs (Caleb Douglas first, then Chris Bell out of Louisville).
Miami is projected to have 450+ pass attempts this year and Malik Willis is the starter.

In Malik Willis's start against the Ravens last year, before he left in the second half injured, Christian Watson had 5 catches for 113 yards, Romeo Doubs 3 for 62, and Jayden Reed 4 for 41 — in roughly 2.5-3 quarters.

Denzel Boston is the Browns' second-round rookie (top of round 2) out of Washington, available in ~75% of leagues, going 159th overall as WR59; 11 college TDs last year with 800+ receiving yards in each of his last two seasons on 25% and 26.5% target shares.

Matt Harmon's Reception Perception on Denzel Boston: 72% success vs man, 72% vs press, strong on in-breaking routes, positional flexibility beyond X; comp family of Michael Pittman, Tetairoa McMillan and Drake London.
Cleveland released Cedric Tillman, leaving the WR room as Denzel Boston (X), KC Concepcion (slot), Jerry Jeudy, and Isaiah Bond as WR4, with Tylan Wallace and Malachi Corley behind them.
Dontayvion Wicks was traded from Green Bay to Philadelphia for a fourth-round pick; he is undrafted in fantasy at WR70 / 223rd overall and available in 91% of leagues.

Dontayvion Wicks career line: rookie year 58 targets, 39 catches, career-high 581 yards with 2.0+ yards per route run (23rd in the NFL) and top-20 in first downs per route run; 2024 was 39 catches on 76 targets with a league-leading drop rate; last year a career-low 46 targets.

Eagles rookie WR Makai Lemon (first-round pick) missed three weeks with a hamstring and is still ramping up; Wicks is reportedly beating out Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Lemon for the WR2 job opposite DeVonta Smith. New Eagles OC (ASR 'Shawn Manion') is running more play action and motion.
Rashid Shaheed is available in 60% of leagues, goes 146th overall as WR56 (12th-13th round); Sal drafted him in the 11th round of the Flock League.
Rashid Shaheed last season: 18 games (no bye after the midseason trade), 92 targets, 687 receiving yards, two receiving TDs, WR48 finish; 10 total receiving TDs over the last three years.

Shaheed split: in his first nine games with New Orleans he averaged 7.3 targets and almost 12 fantasy points per game; in his final nine games after the trade to Seattle, 2.8 targets and 5.8 fantasy points per game.
Seattle traded a fourth and a fifth for Shaheed last year and signed him to a three-year extension adding $35M for a total of over $50M.

De'Zhaun Stribling was the first pick of round 2 to the 49ers out of Ole Miss, is 23, spent five years at three colleges, and posted 800 receiving yards on a 15% target share last year and 892 yards on a 21% target share in 2024.

Ryan Pignetti: he is the first player in at least 20 years with 11 catches inside the first 20 minutes of two consecutive preseason games (next closest: Dez Bryant 10 in 2013, Demaryius Thomas 10 in 2014, Jeremy Maclin 10 in 2015).

Stribling is available in 45% of leagues, goes as a top-100 player / WR40 / eighth-round pick, and was held out of the final preseason game as one of the starters Shanahan sat; Matt Barrows expects a major week-1 role vs the Rams.

49ers pass-catcher status: Ricky Pearsall is done for the year, Christian Kirk has been hurt all camp and may not make the team, Deebo Samuel is 30+, George Kittle is 33 and activated off PUP after a torn Achilles, Mike Evans is 33 with hamstring injuries in four of his last five seasons and missed half of last year.

Turf toe is by definition a sprain of the big toe, so 'toe sprain, not turf toe' resolves nothing — the real question is which toe, and the functional tell is whether the player can cut on it.

Colston Loveland played 81% of Chicago's dropbacks over the final five games with a 31% target-per-route rate and 2.34 yards per route run; Chicago was 6th in 12-personnel and 2nd in 13-personnel over that stretch.
Luther Burden III posted the third-best rookie yards per route run of any wideout since 2011 (min 100 routes) and ranked 2nd in YPRR and 5th in PPR points per route run from week 11 on.
Alec Pierce signed for $114M — the highest-paid free-agent receiver in NFL history at signing — and ran 55% of his routes as digs/ins/crossers/gos, not just gos.

Of every 1,000-yard receiver in the last five years, the only ones drafted later the following season than Alec Pierce is now were a 34-year-old Adam Thielen, a 32-year-old DeAndre Hopkins, a 33-year-old Stefon Diggs and a just-traded Wan'Dale Robinson.
